newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares close sharply up on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares close sharply up on foreign buying.

text.p: Jakarta shares ended sharply higher on Monday as foreign investors re-entered the market and bought selected heavyweights, broker said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 7.65 points, or 1.34 percent, to close at 578.31 points. Gainers led losers by 58 to 28, with 60 counters unchanged.

"Psychologically, today's rise in the index will lend a positive tone to market sentiment on Tuesday, I guess. But the volume will likely remain thin," a broker of a London-based securities house said.
Brokers said overall trade was slow but well-supported by local-led buying of some medium-sized issues coupled with selective foreign buying.
Brokers said the major focus, however, was on the public offering by Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) from Monday to Thursday.
BNI is offering about 1.1 billion shares with an offer price of 850 rupiah ahead its November 25 listing on the Jakarta and Surabaya exhanges.
The market's keystone telecommunications firm Telkom, rose 75 to 3,600 rupiah on a volume of 893,000 shares.
